subject: acoustics

resources.title: Introduction to Oscillations and Waves
resources.notes: High-school-level bridge into oscillations and waves; useful foundation without overstating acoustics specialization.

resources.title: Physics III: Vibrations and Waves
resources.notes: Rigorous vibrations, resonance, wave equations, traveling waves and sound-wave foundations.

resources.title: Acoustics of Speech and Hearing
resources.notes: Graduate acoustics course covering sound measurement, propagation, diffraction, psychoacoustics, electro-acoustic circuits, transducers, hearing and speech.

resources.title: Wave Propagation
resources.notes: Graduate theoretical wave analysis including sound in fluids, geometrical acoustics, scattering, dispersion and energy transport.

resources.title: Computational Ocean Acoustics
resources.notes: Advanced propagation, scattering, reverberation and numerical modeling for ocean acoustic waveguides; supports research preparation but does not alone establish expert readiness.

resources.title: Dynamic Mechanical Metrology: Acceleration, Force, and Acoustics
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: NIST primary standards, calibration and traceability work for acoustic and vibration measurements.

resources.title: NIST Acoustics Resources
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology

resources.title: Acoustical Society of America
resources.notes: Professional society reference; standards and publications retain their own access rights.

resources.title: SciPy Signal Processing
resources.notes: Numerical signal-processing reference for analysis and filtering workflows.

resources.title: librosa Documentation
resources.notes: Audio and music analysis reference; not a substitute for physical acoustics measurements.

known_gaps: Foundation and beginner coverage remains thin for architectural acoustics, musical acoustics, psychoacoustics, ultrasonics and noise control.
Dedicated architectural-acoustics and ultrasonics curricula still need stronger course-level evidence rather than relying primarily on professional references.
Research repositories, standards and measurement references do not by themselves prove expert readiness; applied projects, verification, retrieval evidence and assessment remain required.
